2) Work details: What exactly did they do? (e.g., “replaced kitchen sink drain and P-trap,” “unclogged main line,” “installed new water heater,” etc.)
3) Problem now: What specifically is unsatisfactory? (e.g., still leaking, clog returned, damage to cabinets/walls, not up to code, unsafe, etc.)
4) Evidence: Do you have photos, videos, a written quote, or text/email messages that show what was promised vs what you got?

If you’d like, you can paste brief answers, and I’ll:
- Draft a clear, firm email/text you can send requesting a full refund of $450
- Include mentions of workmanship standards and reasonable timelines
- Add a short escalation section (mentioning you’ll contact your bank, leave factual reviews, or contact licensing/consumer protection) if they don’t respond or refuse.

I’m contacting you regarding the plumbing work you performed at my home on or around December 1, 2025, at [your address]. I paid approximately $450 for this service.

- [Issue 1]
- [Issue 2, if any]

If we can’t resolve this directly, I’ll need to consider other options, such as disputing the charge with my bank or card provider and sharing an honest review of my experience, and, if applicable, contacting any relevant licensing or consumer protection agencies.

I would prefer to resolve this amicably and directly with you, so I hope we can come to a quick resolution.

Sincerely,  
Jamal Richardson  
[jamal.richardson@gmail.com]  
[Your phone number]
---

If you give me the specifics (what they did, what’s wrong now), I’ll customize this letter exactly to your situation and help you with next steps (bank dispute, documentation, etc.) if they push back.</action>

Here’s how to handle it with your credit card, as simply as possible.

1) Gather quick evidence (don’t overthink it)
- Receipt/statement showing the $450 charge to “Capitol Ridge Plumbing” and the date.
- Any invoice or written description of work (if you have it).
- Photos/video of:
  - Standing water
  - Any visible backup around the basement drain
- Screenshot or copy of the refund request message you’re sending them (and any reply).

2) Contact your card issuer (phone or secure message)
Use the “dispute a charge” or “billing inquiries” number on the back of your card or the app.

Here’s a tight script you can use:

“I’d like to dispute a charge for plumbing service.  
The merchant is ‘Capitol Ridge Plumbing,’ amount $450, charged on or around [exact date from your statement].  
They snaked the main line and replaced a section of drain pipe in my basement. Less than two weeks later, the basement drain is backing up again with sewage smell and standing water. I’ve asked them for a refund because the work was unsatisfactory and did not fix the problem, and I’m not getting a resolution.  

I have photos of the ongoing issue, my receipt, and copies of my messages to the plumber. I’d like to open a dispute for services not rendered as agreed / unsatisfactory services.”

If they ask for more detail, keep it to:
- What was promised: fix main line / basement drain issue
- What actually happened: problem is back in under two weeks, same drain, plus smell/standing water
- That you tried to resolve it directly with Capitol Ridge Plumbing.

3) Timeline and follow‑through
- Ask the bank:
  - “Will you issue a provisional credit?”  
  - “What documents do you need from me, and by when?”
- Upload/email exactly what they ask for (photos, invoice, refund email, etc.).
- Save all responses from Capitol Ridge Plumbing (especially if they admit the problem returned or refuse to fix it).

If you want, paste the exact message you plan to send the plumber and I can tighten it one last notch so it lines up perfectly with what you’ll tell the bank.</action>
